tasks.title: Parsing a semver version
tasks.statement: Write parseVersion(str) → { major, minor, patch, prerelease, build }, or null if the string is not a version. A leading "v" is allowed. major, minor and patch are numbers without leading zeros (except 0 itself). After "-" comes the prerelease: identifiers separated by dots from [0-9A-Za-z-]; numeric identifiers (made only of digits) become numbers, the rest stay strings. After "+" comes build metadata (an array of strings). Empty identifiers are not allowed. Whitespace at the ends is trimmed.
tasks.hint: One regular expression with three number groups and two optional tails.

tasks.title: Comparing versions
tasks.statement: Write compare(a, b) → -1, 0 or 1 following semver rules. Versions are strings (parseVersion is already in the starter). First major, minor, patch, compared as numbers. A version without a prerelease is greater than one with a prerelease. Prereleases are compared identifier by identifier from left to right: numeric ones as numbers, string ones lexicographically, and a numeric identifier is lower than a string one; if all shared identifiers are equal, the one with fewer identifiers is lower. Build metadata (+…) is ignored. An invalid version throws TypeError('Invalid Version: ' + the string).
tasks.hint: Numbers first, then a separate function that compares prerelease arrays.

tasks.title: Sorting versions
tasks.statement: Write sortVersions(list, desc = false): it returns a new array of version strings sorted by semver (ascending; descending when desc is set). Invalid versions are skipped. Versions of equal precedence (differing only in build metadata) keep their original order. The functions parseVersion and compare are already in the starter.
tasks.hint: filter(parseVersion), then sort with compare; for desc flip the sign.

tasks.title: Version ranges
tasks.statement: Write satisfies(version, range). A range is one or more sets separated by "||"; a set is comparators separated by spaces (AND) or a hyphen range "A - B". A comparator is "^", "~", ">=", ">", "<=", "<", "=", or no operator, plus a partial version ("1", "1.2", "1.2.3", "1.x", "*"). Rules: "^1.2.3" = >=1.2.3 <2.0.0; "^0.2.3" = >=0.2.3 <0.3.0; "^0.0.3" = >=0.0.3 <0.0.4; "~1.2.3" = >=1.2.3 <1.3.0; "~1" = >=1.0.0 <2.0.0; "1.x" and "1" — >=1.0.0 <2.0.0; "1.2" — >=1.2.0 <1.3.0; "*" — anything. A version with a prerelease matches a set only if the set has a comparator with the same major.minor.patch and a prerelease. parseVersion and compare are already there.
tasks.hint: Expand each comparator into pairs (operator, version) and check them all; then apply the prerelease rule.

tasks.title: Highest matching version
tasks.statement: Write maxSatisfying(versions, range): the version from the list with the highest semver precedence that matches range; null if none match. Invalid versions are skipped. Prereleases are chosen only if the range allows them (the rule: the set contains a comparator with the same major.minor.patch and a prerelease). The starter has parseVersion, compare and satisfies for the ranges ^, ~, >=, >, <=, <, exact versions, "*" and a space as AND.
tasks.hint: Filter with satisfies, then take the maximum by cmpV.

tasks.title: Incrementing a version
tasks.statement: Write inc(version, kind, id = 'alpha'): kind is 'major', 'minor', 'patch' or 'prerelease'. For major/minor/patch: if the version has a prerelease and the reset is already "in place" (for major: minor = patch = 0; for minor: patch = 0; for patch — always), just drop the prerelease; otherwise increment the needed part and zero the lower ones, removing the prerelease and metadata. For prerelease: with no prerelease, increment patch and append "-id.0"; with a prerelease whose first identifier equals id and whose last one is a number, increment that number; with any other prerelease, replace it with "id.0" (the major.minor.patch numbers don't change). The result is a string without "+build". An invalid version gives null.
tasks.hint: Parse the version with a regular expression and build the string by hand.

tasks.title: Kind of version difference
tasks.statement: Write diff(a, b): it returns 'major', 'minor', 'patch', 'prerelease' or null (the versions are equal; build metadata is ignored). Versions are compared by precedence: if major differs — 'major', otherwise if minor differs — 'minor', otherwise if patch differs — 'patch'; if the numbers are equal but the prereleases differ — 'prerelease'. If one of the versions has a prerelease and differs from the other in its numbers, the kind is determined by the most significant differing part ("1.0.0-rc.1" and "2.0.0" — 'major'). It doesn't depend on argument order. An invalid version throws TypeError.
tasks.hint: Parse both versions with parseV and compare the parts in order.

tasks.title: Parsing "name@range"
tasks.statement: Write parsePackageSpec(spec) → { name, range }, or null. The name is "name" or "@scope/name" (exactly one part after "@scope/"); after the name comes an optional "@range". If there is no range or it is empty, range = 'latest'. The range may contain any characters (except whitespace at the start and end, which is trimmed). An empty string, "@" without a name, "@scope" without "/name", and a name with spaces all give null.

tasks.title: Validating a package name
tasks.statement: Write validatePackageName(name) → { valid, errors }. errors is an array of strings in the order of the checks: "name must be a string" (not a string — return immediately); "name length must be greater than zero" (empty); "name can no longer contain more than 214 characters"; "name cannot start with a period" ("."); "name cannot start with an underscore"; "name can no longer contain capital letters" (contains A–Z); "name can only contain URL-friendly characters" (after stripping the "@scope/" prefix, characters outside [a-z0-9._~-] remain, in lower case; spaces, "/", "!" and so on); "name is reserved" (the name equals node_modules or favicon.ico). For a scope "@scope/name", check both the scope and the name as separate parts: each must be non-empty; otherwise "name must be a valid scoped name".
tasks.hint: First split off the scope, then apply the checks to the name one by one.

tasks.title: Dependency resolution and hoisting
tasks.statement: Write resolveTree(registry, rootDeps). registry is { name: { version: { dependencies: { name: range } } } }, rootDeps is { name: range } (ranges like ^, ~, exact, *). The result is an object "install path → version" with sorted keys. Algorithm: a queue of requests {name, range, dir}; the root requests are sorted by name, with dir = '' (the root). To process a request, walk up from dir through its parents (dir, then its parent, …, the root) and find the first package already installed at the path `${d}node_modules/${name}`; if one exists and its version matches, the request is satisfied. Otherwise pick the highest matching version from registry (none — Error('No matching version for name@range')) and install it in the topmost directory, going from the root down to dir, where the slot `node_modules/name` is free (if none are free — Error('Unresolvable')). After installing, put requests for its dependencies (in order of name) at the end of the queue, with dir = the path of its directory `${slot}/` (for example 'node_modules/a/'). An install path looks like "node_modules/a" or "node_modules/a/node_modules/b"; a package's directory dir is the path + '/'. The starter has satisfies/cmpV/parseV for ^, ~, exact versions, >=, <, *.
tasks.hint: BFS over the request queue; the function ancestors(dir) returns the chain of directories from dir to the root, and for installing — from the root to dir.

tasks.title: Dependency cycles
tasks.statement: Write findCycles(graph): graph is { node: [dependencies] } (the dependencies may include nodes that are not among the keys). It returns an array of cycles: each cycle is a strongly connected group of nodes of size ≥ 2, or a node that refers to itself; inside a group the names are sorted alphabetically; the groups are sorted by their first name. If there are no cycles, return an empty array.
tasks.hint: Tarjan's algorithm (strongly connected components) or mutual reachability.

tasks.title: Install order
tasks.statement: Write installOrder(graph): graph is { package: [dependencies] }. Return an array of all packages (the keys and the dependencies mentioned) in install order: each dependency comes before the package that depends on it. Among the packages available to install (all dependencies already installed) always pick the first alphabetically. On a cycle, throw Error('cycle: ' + the remaining packages joined with ", " in alphabetical order).
tasks.hint: Kahn's algorithm, choosing the smallest name at every step.

tasks.title: Duplicates in the tree
tasks.statement: Write findDuplicates(tree): tree is { install path: version } (for example "node_modules/a/node_modules/c": "1.0.0"). The package name is the part after the last "node_modules/". Return an object "name → array of versions" only for packages installed in two or more different versions; the versions have no repeats and are sorted by semver (ascending); the keys are in alphabetical order. The functions parseV and cmpV for comparing versions are already there.
tasks.hint: Group by name, collect a Set of versions, filter size > 1, sort with cmpV.

tasks.title: Serializing a lock file
tasks.statement: Write serializeLock(tree) (node:crypto): tree is { install path: version }. The result is a JSON string indented by 2 spaces: { "lockfileVersion": 1, "packages": { path: { "version": v, "integrity": i } } } — the paths sorted alphabetically. integrity = "sha256-" + base64(sha256 of the string `${name}@${version}`), where name is the part after the last "node_modules/". The string ends with a newline.
tasks.hint: createHash('sha256').update(...).digest('base64'); JSON.stringify(obj, null, 2) + '\n'.

tasks.title: Checking the lock file (npm ci)
tasks.statement: Write checkLock(manifest, lock): manifest is { dependencies, devDependencies }, lock is { packages: { path: { version } } }. For each dependency from both sections (the name is the key), check the root install lock.packages['node_modules/name']. If it is missing — "name: missing from lock". If it exists but the version doesn't satisfy the range — "name: lock has VERSION, manifest wants RANGE" (substitute the actual version and range). Return an array of problems sorted by string. satisfies, parseV and cmpV are already in the starter.
tasks.hint: Merge dependencies and devDependencies; if names coincide, check both ranges (two problems are possible).

tasks.title: Lock file difference
tasks.statement: Write diffLock(oldTree, newTree): the trees are { install path: version }. The result is { added, removed, changed }: added — strings "path@version" for paths that didn't exist before; removed — "path@version" for paths that disappeared; changed — objects { path, from, to } for paths with a different version. All lists are sorted by path.
tasks.hint: Take the union of the keys, sort, and branch on presence in both trees.

tasks.title: Pre and post hooks
tasks.statement: Write scriptPlan(scripts, name): it returns an array of script names in execution order: "pre" + name (if it exists), name, "post" + name (if it exists). If the script name doesn't exist, throw Error('Missing script: ' + name). Hooks have no hooks of their own: scriptPlan(s, 'prebuild') returns only ['prebuild'] (if it exists).
tasks.hint: Check existence with Object.hasOwn; add hooks only for the requested name.

tasks.title: PATH for scripts
tasks.statement: Write binPath(cwd, pathEnv): cwd is an absolute path (POSIX, no trailing "/" except for the root "/"), pathEnv is the value of PATH (it may be an empty string or undefined). Return a string: for each ancestor directory, from cwd up to and including the root — "<directory>/node_modules/.bin" (for the root — "/node_modules/.bin"), then the elements of the original PATH; everything joined with ":". An empty PATH adds no empty elements.
tasks.hint: Walk upward over split('/'); for the root the directory is an empty string.

tasks.title: The workspace: protocol
tasks.statement: Write resolveWorkspaceRefs(pkgs): pkgs is { name: { version, dependencies } }. Return a new structure of the same shape in which the "workspace:…" values in dependencies are replaced with real ones: "workspace:*" → the exact version of the dependency package from pkgs; "workspace:^" → "^version"; "workspace:~" → "~version"; "workspace:range" → the range itself. If the package is not in pkgs, throw Error('Workspace package not found: ' + name). Leave other values unchanged and do not mutate the original objects.
tasks.hint: For each dependency: if the value starts with "workspace:", cut off the prefix and examine the rest.

tasks.title: Contents of a published package
tasks.statement: Write packFiles(allFiles, pkg): allFiles are the project's file paths (POSIX, relative), pkg.files is an optional array of patterns: an exact path ("index.js"), a directory ("dist" — everything inside it), or "*.ext" (files with that extension in the root, no nested directories). Always included: package.json and files in the root whose name (without extension, case-insensitive) is README or LICENSE or LICENCE. Always excluded: everything inside node_modules/ and .git/, ".DS_Store" files (in any directory) and files ending in "~". If pkg.files is not set, all files are included except the excluded ones. The result is sorted.
tasks.hint: Exclusions first, then the always-included, then the files patterns.

tasks.title: Checking peerDependencies
tasks.statement: Write checkPeers(installed, packages): installed is { name: version }, packages is { name: { peerDependencies: { peer: range } } } (for installed packages). For each installed package and each of its peers: if the peer is not in installed — "package: missing peer peer@range"; if the peer's version doesn't satisfy — "package: peer peer@range but VERSION installed" (substitute the actual names, range and version). The result is a sorted array of strings. The helpers satisfies/parseV/cmpV are already there.
tasks.hint: Iterate over packages (only those present in installed).

tasks.title: Outdated dependencies
tasks.statement: Write outdated(installed, latest): installed and latest are { name: version } (no prereleases). Return an array of { name, current, latest, type } for packages where latest is newer than current; type is 'major', 'minor' or 'patch' according to the most significant differing part. Sort by name. Packages with no entry in latest are skipped. The helpers parseV and cmpV are already there.
tasks.hint: Compare cmpV(latest, current) > 0; the type is the first differing one of major/minor/patch.

tasks.title: Audit report
tasks.statement: Write audit(installed, advisories): installed is { name: version }, advisories is an array of { id, name, range, severity } (severity: low, moderate, high, critical; range is the range of vulnerable versions). Return { vulnerabilities, counts }. vulnerabilities — for each pair (package, advisory) where the installed version falls within range: { name, version, id, severity }; sorted by descending severity (critical → low), then by name, then by id. counts is { low, moderate, high, critical }: the number of vulnerabilities of each severity (zeros included). satisfies, parseV and cmpV are already there.
tasks.hint: Severity ranks for sorting: critical 0, high 1, moderate 2, low 3.

tasks.title: Update policy
tasks.statement: Write pickUpdate(current, available, policy): available is an array of versions, policy is 'patch', 'minor' or 'latest'. Pick the highest version from available that is strictly newer than current and allowed by the policy: 'patch' — the same major and minor; 'minor' — the same major; 'latest' — any. Prereleases (versions with "-") and invalid versions are not considered. If nothing fits — null. The helpers parseV and cmpV are there.
tasks.hint: Filter by the policy and by cmpV, then take the maximum.

tasks.title: Tree size and duplicates
tasks.statement: Write treeSize(tree, sizes): tree is { install path: version }, sizes is { 'name@version': bytes } (the name is the part after the last "node_modules/"). The result: { total, unique, wasted }. total is the sum of sizes over all install paths; unique is the number of distinct "name@version"; wasted is total minus the sum of the sizes of the distinct "name@version" (that is, the space taken by extra copies). If a size is missing from sizes, count it as 0.
tasks.hint: A Map/Set of distinct keys; accumulate total over the paths.

tasks.title: Finding phantom dependencies
tasks.statement: Write findPhantoms(imports, manifest, hoisted): imports are specifiers from the code ("zod", "zod/v3", "@scope/pkg/x", "./local", "node:fs", "fs"); manifest is { dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies }; hoisted is an array of package names physically present in the root node_modules. For each unique package name from imports (the name is "x" or "@s/x", without the subpath; relative "./", "../", "/" and "node:…" are ignored, as are the built-in modules fs, path, os, http, crypto, util, url, events, stream) that is not declared in the manifest — { name, reason }: reason is 'hoisted' if the name is in hoisted (the import works by accident), otherwise 'missing'. The result is sorted by name.
tasks.hint: Extract the package name with a regular expression, collect a Set, check the declarations.

tasks.title: A package's exports map
tasks.statement: Write resolveExports(exports, subpath, conditions). exports is a string (the same as { '.': string }), a conditions object (keys without "." — the same as { '.': object }) or a subpath map (keys start with "."). subpath is '.' or './something'. The target is a string, a conditions object or null. In a conditions object go through the keys in the order written: a key matches if it is 'default' or one of conditions — take its value (recursively, if it is an object); if no key matched, throw an error. The subpath is looked up first exactly, then by a pattern with "*" (a key like './features/*' — the matched part is substituted for "*" in the target). If the subpath doesn't exist or the target is null — Error('Package subpath "' + subpath + '" is not defined by "exports"').
tasks.hint: Normalize exports to a subpath map; then write a function target(value, conditions) for the conditions.

tasks.title: Parsing .npmrc
tasks.statement: Write parseNpmrc(text, env). Lines of the form "key=value" (whitespace around is trimmed); lines starting with ";" or "#", and empty ones, are skipped. In values "${NAME}" is replaced with env[NAME] (if missing — an empty string). The result is { registry, scopes, auth, other }: "registry=URL" → registry; "@scope:registry=URL" → scopes['@scope']; "//host/path/:_authToken=T" → auth['//host/path/'] = T; the other pairs go into other. registry defaults to 'https://registry.npmjs.org/'. When a key repeats, the last one wins.
tasks.hint: Split into lines, find the first "=", then classify the key.

tasks.title: Content-addressed store (like pnpm)
tasks.statement: Write addToStore(store, files) (node:crypto): store is an object "sha256 hash (hex) → size in bytes", files is { path: content string }. For each file compute the sha256 hex of the UTF-8 content. Return { paths, added, saved }: paths is { path: hash }; added is the number of files that were not in store (and they are added to store with their size in bytes); saved is the total size of files that were already in store or repeated within files (that is, what didn't have to be stored again). Files are processed in key order.
tasks.hint: Buffer.byteLength(content); if the hash is already in store, saved += size, otherwise store[hash] = size.

tasks.title: Validating package.json
tasks.statement: Write validateManifest(pkg) → a sorted array of error strings: "name: required" (missing or not a non-empty string); "version: invalid semver" (no version of the form x.y.z[-pre][+build] — "required" is not needed, a missing version is also "invalid semver"); for each key K in dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies, where the value is not a string — "SECTION.K: must be a string" (SECTION is the section name, for example "dependencies.K"); for each script — "scripts.K: must be a string"; "main: must be a string" (if main is set and is not a string); "type: must be \"module\" or \"commonjs\"" (if set and different); "private: must be a boolean" (if set and not a boolean). A section that is not an object gives "SECTION: must be an object" (instead of checking its keys).
tasks.hint: Collect errors with push, and call sort() at the end.
